hook.text: Temperature rises and defects increase. Is heat the cause? A scatter diagram shows the relationship instantly.

buildup.text: Scatter diagrams plot two variables against each other to reveal whether they're related.

discovery.text: A clear upward or downward pattern suggests correlation. A random cloud means the variables aren't linked.

twist.text: Correlation doesn't prove causation. Ice cream sales and drownings both rise in summer—but ice cream doesn't kill.

climax.text: Used alongside root cause analysis, scatter diagrams help teams test whether their theories are supported by data.

punchline.text: Plot the dots. See if the pattern is real.

quiz.question: What does a scatter diagram reveal?
